title: Taking an Uber, Part 3: Stuck in the Jam
culturalNote: The Uber is back — and so is Kamau, your driver from Parts 1 and 2. Monday-morning traffic on Waiyaki Way is legendary, and drivers know every shortcut (njia ya mkato) through the leafy back roads of Lavington. Small talk in a jam is normal and expected. This time the conversation is about what already happened: the weekend, the accident, the missed call. That's the past tense -li-, and its negative -ku-.
startingPoint: Monday, 7:20 a.m. You order an Uber to the office — and Kamau pulls up again.
